subject: Film & Cinema
title: The Polish Film School
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Polish Film School.

hook.text: Behind the Iron Curtain, Polish filmmakers smuggled dissent into state-funded cinema.

buildup.text: Directors like Andrzej Wajda explored WWII trauma and moral compromise under occupation.

discovery.text: Their films used allegory to criticize the Soviet system without being overtly political.

twist.text: The government funded the very films that subtly undermined its authority.

climax.text: The Polish School influenced filmmakers across Eastern Europe and laid groundwork for Solidarity.

punchline.text: The state paid for its own critique.

quiz.question: How did Polish Film School directors criticize the Soviet system?
options: Through allegory embedded in historical stories
